story-0002feeb5ff9dca098815194.content: As predicted: UK Parliamentarians are agitating for mandatory “Spyware” on all phones, computers, and tablets: on the pretext of detecting Indecent Images of Children (CSAM). This might sound like a laudable objective: “The campaign asks for a requirement in primary legislation that the operating systems of phones, tablets and laptops sold in the UK block child sexual abuse material on the device; scope limited to that material, with any change needing a vote of Parliament; independent testing before and after deployment, with the results published; and a criminal offence for any other use. Apple, Google and Meta already run on-device software that recognises and blurs nudity, including inside encrypted messages, as an optional setting for children’s accounts.” However, this is state-sponsored device-level surveillance of every connected device owner’s photos, videos, and livestreams. That means the government is sifting through legal, consensual, adult nudes in every owner’s photo gallery, emails, and messages using fallible technology. Apple’s new UK terms and conditions already include being restricted, suspended, or banned from using Apple “Software or Services”. The implications for freedom of expression, to freely send and receive information, might lead to self-censorship at best; and slippage towards total client-side scanning (looking at everything on a user’s phone) at worst. This is a simply unacceptable intrusion into individuals’ liberties. This should be of concern to everyone, from victims of sexual violence in possession of evidence of their assaults; adult-content creators, whether sex workers, or amateurs filming consensual adult liaisons; and consumers of legal adult content.

Energy Aspects will be in Vienna, 10–12 November, showcasing how these capabilities are transforming the way the energy industry monitors infrastructure, tracks activity and anticipates developments on the ground. Our capabilities span: - Data Center Monitoring: Near-real-time visibility into US data center build-out and the power plants behind it. - Crude Oil Intelligence: Satellite-enabled visibility into global oil infrastructure and activity. - LNG Intelligence: Geospatial insights into LNG infrastructure and market developments. - E&P Intelligence: Earth Observation data supporting upstream energy analysis. - Methane Watch: Satellite-based insights into methane emissions and environmental risks. - FireWatch: Geospatial monitoring of fires and risks to energy infrastructure. SPACE DATA. EARTH INSIGHTS. ENERGY INTELLIGENCE. Meet our team in Vienna: Johannes Gross, Capt. Adrian Ratiu and Florian Thaler. Discover how satellite technology, AI and advanced geospatial analytics are opening new frontiers in energy intelligence. story-02f737b5c49ee325a8349419.content: RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/6TtNq3sWP5 | Author: @militarnyi Spain Develops EO Master Platform for Automated Intelligence With Satellite Imagery Spanish company INTEGRASYS has unveiled EO Master – a platform for object recognition in geospatial intelligence (GEOINT). The tool applies artificial intelligence and machine learning to optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery, the company told Militarnyi. The system’s main advantage is the full automation of routine intelligence tasks, eliminating the need for operators to manually review imagery. Instead of analysts manually searching for military equipment at airfields or positions, EO Master does it automatically. The platform compares detected objects against an extensive library of 3D models, including those of the latest military equipment. This allows the system to quickly and accurately distinguish actual combat vehicles, ships and aircraft from mock-ups and false targets. Interface of EO Master by INTEGRASYS Specialists can set recognition confidence thresholds for each object class. The system allows users to identify targets down to the specific aircraft type and its position on the parking lot, while simultaneously monitoring multiple locations and imagery dates through user-friendly dashboards. The results of automated processing can be exported as KML files or compiled into proprietary Earth Observation Report reports. This provides defence and intelligence agencies with a verified documentary record of observation data with precise timestamps. EO Master was first launched more than two and a half years ago, in March 2024, at the SATELLITE exhibition in Washington, D.C. Since its launch, the developers have continuously expanded the platform’s capabilities, adding military equipment recognition across the air, maritime and ground domains. Interface of EO Master by INTEGRASYS The tool is already integrated into the operations of defence ministries and intelligence agencies in several NATO countries. “In addition, EO Master is already integrated into a unified interface with two other INTEGRASYS modules: INTEGEO, which combines signal geolocation data, and AIS, which is used for vessel tracking,” the company emphasised. Military personnel consider the platform important because it allows data to be transmitted to frontline troops’ tablets while using minimal bandwidth. This significantly shortens the kill chain. #Ukraine #Russia #Drones #UAV #FPV

story-045f1db202006459223bfa51.content: ورقة علمية صادمة من جامعة ييل تشهد إثباتاً رياضياً: الذكاء الاصطناعي يستعد لإبادة الطبقة المتوسطة نهائياً! 🚨 ​الورقة أعدت نموذجاً اقتصادياً لما سيحدث للاقتصاد العالمي عندما يصل الذكاء الاصطناعي العام (AGI) إلى وضعه النهائي.. والنتائج تبين أن القوانين الاقتصادية التاريخية على وشك الانقلاب للأبد! 💥👇 ​1️⃣ القيمة الفعالية لعملك = سعر الـ GPU! راتبك لن يعتمد بعد اليوم على شهادتك الجامعة، أو سنوات خبرتك، أو ندرة مهاراتك.. قيمتك المالية ستحدد رياضياً بتكلفة الحوسبة والطاقة (GPU Compute) المطلوبة لاستبدالك! إذا كان هناك وكيل ذكاء اصطناعي يعمل بـ 2 دولار كهرباء وحوسبة لينجز مهامك اليومية، فإن قيمتك الاقتصادية ستسقف رسمياً عند 2 دولار فقط! ⚡️💀 ​2️⃣ موت مفهوم "رأس المال البشري": الدراسة تؤكد أن القيمة المالية للعمل البشري تتجه رياضياً نحو الصفر؛ لو توقف 50% من البشر عن العمل غداً، لن ينخفض الناتج المحلي الإجمالي العالمي بنسبة 1%، بل يستمر في النمو المتسارع لأن المحركات الحقيقية أصبحت الشريحة والكهرباء والخوارزميات! ​3️⃣ التحول من التداول بالوقت إلى حيازة الحوسبة: المجتمع ينتقل بالكامل من نظام قائم على "الجهد البشري" إلى نظام قائم على "رأس مال الحوسبة" (Compute Capital). إذا كانت مهاراتك قابلة للمحاكاة على خوادم، فسينتهي نفوذك الاقتصادي تماماً! البشر يُطردون تدريجياً من النظام الاقتصادي الذي بنوه بأيديهم لصالح السيليكون.. النموذج ينهي رسمياً حقبة "تداول الوقت مقابل المال"! 🤯 سحق الطبقة المتوسطة لم يعد مجرد تخوف، بل معادلة رياضية مثبتة!

story-058e87342c0e8472b79ca7a8.content: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman. At least four vessels, including three U.S.-sanctioned tankers, have reportedly slowed down, circled cable routes and switched off their tracking systems at unusual moments. Maritime intelligence firm Windward says their movements are consistent with potentially mapping cable locations or placing explosives, although no sabotage has been confirmed. The activity follows explicit warnings from Iran's Revolutionary Guard that underwater internet cables, AI facilities and data centers could become targets if the U.S. and Israel launch another bombing campaign. The stakes are enormous. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar depend entirely on cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz for international internet connectivity. Damaging them could disrupt banking transactions, communications, cloud computing and digital businesses across the Gulf. With Washington continuing to move military assets toward the region, Tehran appears to be signaling that another war could threaten far more than oil shipments. Source: Financial Times / Writer: Mhedi

story-063d3ba3756e383844cbee90.content: Russian Satellites Aid Iranian Proxies in Strikes on Saudi Arabia — AP ▪️ Last month, Iranian-backed armed groups carried out a precision strike, hitting pumping stations along a critical Saudi Arabian oil pipeline. A few days later, another strike targeted a Saudi military airbase, damaging an Italian-made fighter jet housed in a hangar. ▪️ Russian reconnaissance satellites—specifically the "Kosmos-2600"—played a crucial role in the success of these strikes, hovering over the key targets shortly before the attacks took place. ▪️ A private geospatial intelligence firm analyzed 40 missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia—carried out by Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and armed groups in Iraq between July 1 and October 19. In every instance, the firm identified a consistent pattern: Russian government and military satellites were orbiting over these areas in the days leading up to and following the attacks. ▪️ Three officials—including a Saudi representative and a senior member of the Houthi leadership—along with a private intelligence analyst, told the Associated Press that the Houthis and other Iranian allies have utilized intelligence provided by Russia, as well as capabilities from China. According to the AP, Iranian advisors on the ground analyzed intelligence and passed it on to their allies.

story-09d07d6b7b2591948cddd64f.content: Someone built an open-source tool to make your smart TV feel like a clean, premium device again. 📺 No endless recommendations. No crowded home screen. No unnecessary preinstalled apps. It's called CleanYourTV, and it uses developer tools and AI coding assistants to simplify Android and Google TV devices. The project was originally created by developer Gathin to make his parents' television easier to use. Now it's available for everyone. ✨ What does it actually do? ▪️ Simplifies your home screen: Replaces the busy default interface with a lightweight, customizable launcher. ▪️ Disables unnecessary packages: Identifies optional telemetry, recommendations, and preinstalled software that can be disabled. ▪️ Keeps your essential apps: You can retain the streaming services and other applications you actually use. ▪️ Creates backups: Saves package information so changes can be reviewed or reversed. ▪️ Works without root: Uses Android Debug Bridge (ADB) over your local network. The distinction matters: CleanYourTV generally disables system packages rather than permanently uninstalling them. That makes the changes easier to reverse, although disabling the wrong package can still cause problems. 🤖 Where does AI come in? The project includes a workflow that can be used with coding assistants such as Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI. An agent can help inspect your television's software, identify unnecessary packages, and walk through the cleanup process. You don't need to write a custom Android application or manually research every package. 🔧 What you'll need ▪️ An Android TV or Google TV device. ▪️ A computer connected to the same local network. ▪️ Developer options and debugging temporarily enabled on the television. ▪️ A supported agent or the project's installation instructions. The developer describes the process as taking around 15 minutes, although actual setup time depends on your device. ⚠️ Important limitations This isn't a universal smart TV tool. Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, Roku, and VIDAA aren't supported. It also doesn't remove advertisements embedded inside streaming apps. The main focus is the Android TV environment itself. And after finishing, it's sensible to disable debugging again. Why this matters Smart TVs often become slower and more cluttered as manufacturers add recommendations, promotions, and background services. CleanYourTV offers a way to take back control of that experience without buying new hardware. The project is free and MIT-licensed. 🔗 https://t.co/VJQFJ7ETx9 🔗 https://t.co/f19V5AIZDX #AndroidTV #OpenSource #SmartTV #AIAgents

story-0a6cbcd35e3f61f282fd64bf.content: Claude Code just found out that your smart TV can quietly take screenshots of whatever you’re watching, even in the middle of your favorite series. Texas sued five TV makers over it, and one class action says it happens every 500 milliseconds. I asked Claude Code to dig into how it works, how to protect yourself, and how to turn it off.👇 The feature is called ACR, Automatic Content Recognition. Over and over, your TV grabs a tiny sample of the picture or sound and turns it into a short fingerprint. It sends that fingerprint to a server, which matches it against a huge database of shows, movies, channels and ads. The server answers something like "this is Show X, episode 4, minute 14", and that gets added to a viewing profile. Companies use those profiles to measure which ads people saw and to target ads at you. This is not new, and it has been in court before. In 2017 the FTC and New Jersey went after Vizio, saying it collected viewing histories from 11 million smart TVs. Vizio paid $2.2 million to settle. In December 2025 the Texas Attorney General sued five TV makers: Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense and TCL. The lawsuit accuses them of running "mass surveillance programs" that build viewer profiles for advertising without meaningful consent. He calls the practice "watchware". In 2026 Samsung settled in Texas. It agreed to stop collecting ACR data from Texans without explicit, informed consent, and to rewrite its on-screen privacy prompts. Separately, a class action in New York alleges Samsung's ACR records image and audio every 500 milliseconds, even when the TV is used as a PC monitor. That is an allegation, not a court finding. Most people never noticed because ACR is usually switched on during setup, inside a long agreement nobody reads. The setting names sound harmless: "Viewing Information Services", "Live Plus", "Viewing Data". And not every TV does this. It depends on brand, model and region. Here is where to turn it off (menus vary by model and year): Samsung: Settings → Support → Terms & Privacy → Privacy Choices → turn off Viewing Information Services LG: All Settings → General → System → Additional Settings → turn off Live Plus Vizio: Menu → System → Reset & Admin → turn off Viewing Data Roku TVs: Settings → Privacy → Smart TV Experience → turn off "Use info from TV inputs" Don't see any of these? Look in Privacy, Advertising or Terms of Service for anything about "viewing data" or "interest-based ads". If you can't find it, you can also keep the TV offline and watch through a separate streaming box. Your TV isn't evil. But it's a computer that can see what's on your screen, and the default setting is usually on. Check yours today. Save this for the next time you set up a TV. And tell me: what brand is yours? 👇

story-0c980b0bce3498d02e355321.content: NOW: $500 billion. $200 million. $2 trillion. The AI race has a price list. A former Anthropic researcher says it has no brakes. Jacob Coxon, who says he spent three years researching at Anthropic and OpenAI, put it this way: "We know how to control nuclear weapons... We don't yet know how to control AI." He called it possibly the most dangerous technology humanity has created, and said an international AI arms race would be disastrous. The price list: $500 billion: the headline pledge of Stargate, backed by Trump, OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank. $200 million: the ceiling of each Pentagon AI contract for xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. $2 trillion: the valuation of SpaceX, which owns Elon Musk's AI lab xAI. Trump's line on the race: whoever wins it is probably going to win, period. Coxon says cooperate. Washington says win. Nobody has said who is in control.

U.S. Cyber Command: Directed to prioritize operations against foreign election interference. U.S. Military: Authorized intelligence and cybersecurity capabilities mobilized for election defense. Military AI: Advanced AI-assisted intelligence and cyber capabilities reportedly incorporated into election-security operations. NSA: Foreign cyberthreat detection and intelligence support. DIA: Foreign-threat intelligence collection and analysis. NGA: Geospatial intelligence support. DHS/CISA: Election infrastructure security plan, vulnerability scanning, threat intelligence, and incident-response assistance. FBI: Cybercrime investigations, election-threat reporting, and cybersecurity coordination. ODNI: Foreign election-threat intelligence and interagency assessments. EAC: Voting-system certification, security standards, and AI-related election-security guidance. Federal–State Coordination: Threat-information sharing and election incident-response resources. This was a substantial federal security apparatus. The American public deserves transparency about what these agencies detected, investigated, and ultimately concluded.

story-10bf8449338f19b716b2a5d2.content: Dario Amodei 在国会听证会上把话挑明了： 开源 AI 再这么走下去，会走向极其危险的境地。 他的逻辑很赤裸： 模型握在自己手里，你能监控谁在用、能随时拔掉某个用户的网线，还能随时给模型划定红线。 但一旦开源放出去，这些“刹车片”就全废了： 模型彻底脱手，你再也收不回来。 于是他直接把球踢给了开源阵营：别回避，你们自己想办法兜底。 这番话最狠的地方在于，他几乎不装了： 顶级智能，不该交到所有人手里。 开源和闭源的根本分歧，从来不是技术路线，而是控制权。 一边想死死握住随时叫停的开关，另一边则认为，放出去的火种就不该再由任何人收回。 看到这你就懂了，为什么两派如今势同水火： 这从来不是一场技术辩论，而是一场权力分配。 https://t.co/lBpTLgYz3L

story-125d85bea3320e9784f4d867.content: New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling. Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way. In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support. https://t.co/qsFJG76FDw

story-12f6198d450a2ffad5aafb5d.content:
For much of last year, about 2,500 US service members from the 15th Marine Expeditionary Unit sailed aboard three ships throughout the Pacific, conducting training exercises in the waters off South Korea, the Philippines, India, and Indonesia. At the same time, onboard the ships, an experiment was unfolding: The Marines in the unit responsible for sorting through foreign intelligence and making their superiors aware of possible local threats were for the first time using generative AI to do it, testing a leading AI tool the Pentagon has been funding.

Two officers tell us that they used the new system to help scour thousands of pieces of open-source intelligence—nonclassified articles, reports, images, videos—collected in the various countries where they operated, and that it did so far faster than was possible with the old method of analyzing them manually. Captain Kristin Enzenauer, for instance, says she used large language models to translate and summarize foreign news sources, while Captain Will Lowdon used AI to help write the daily and weekly intelligence reports he provided to his commanders. 

“We still need to validate the sources,” says Lowdon. But the unit’s commanders encouraged the use of large language models, he says, “because they provide a lot more efficiency during a dynamic situation.”

The generative AI tools they used were built by the defense-tech company Vannevar Labs, which in November was granted a production contract worth up to $99 million by the Pentagon’s startup-oriented Defense Innovation Unit with the goal of bringing its intelligence tech to more military units. The company, founded in 2019 by veterans of the CIA and US intelligence community, joins the likes of Palantir, Anduril, and Scale AI as a major beneficiary of the US military’s embrace of artificial intelligence—not only for physical technologies like drones and autonomous vehicles but also for software that is revolutionizing how the Pentagon collects, manages, and interprets data for warfare and surveillance. 

Though the US military has been developing computer vision models and similar AI tools, like those used in Project Maven, since 2017, the use of generative AI—tools that can engage in human-like conversation like those built by Vannevar Labs—represent a newer frontier.

The company applies existing large language models, including some from OpenAI and Microsoft, and some bespoke ones of its own to troves of open-source intelligence the company has been collecting since 2021. The scale at which this data is collected is hard to comprehend (and a large part of what sets Vannevar’s products apart): terabytes of data in 80 different languages are hoovered every day in 180 countries. The company says it is able to analyze social media profiles and breach firewalls in countries like China to get hard-to-access information; it also uses nonclassified data that is difficult to get online (gathered by human operatives on the ground), as well as reports from physical sensors that covertly monitor radio waves to detect illegal shipping activities. 

Vannevar then builds AI models to translate information, detect threats, and analyze political sentiment, with the results delivered through a chatbot interface that’s not unlike ChatGPT. The aim is to provide customers with critical information on topics as varied as international fentanyl supply chains and China’s efforts to secure rare earth minerals in the Philippines. 

“Our real focus as a company,” says Scott Philips, Vannevar Labs’ chief technology officer, is to “collect data, make sense of that data, and help the US make good decisions.” 

That approach is particularly appealing to the US intelligence apparatus because for years the world has been awash in more data than human analysts can possibly interpret—a problem that contributed to the 2003 founding of Palantir, a company with a market value of over $200 billion and known for its powerful and controversial tools, including a database that helps Immigration and Customs Enforcement search for and track information on undocumented immigrants. 

In 2019, Vannevar saw an opportunity to use large language models, which were then new on the scene, as a novel solution to the data conundrum. The technology could enable AI not just to collect data but to actually talk through an analysis with someone interactively.

Vannevar’s tools proved useful for the deployment in the Pacific, and Enzenauer and Lowdon say that while they were instructed to always double-check the AI’s work, they didn’t find inaccuracies to be a significant issue. Enzenauer regularly used the tool to track any foreign news reports in which the unit’s exercises were mentioned and to perform sentiment analysis, detecting the emotions and opinions expressed in text. Judging whether a foreign news article reflects a threatening or friendly opinion toward the unit is a task that on previous deployments she had to do manually.

“It was mostly by hand—researching, translating, coding, and analyzing the data,” she says. “It was definitely way more time-consuming than it was when using the AI.” 

Still, Enzenauer and Lowdon say there were hiccups, some of which would affect most digital tools: The ships had spotty internet connections much of the time, limiting how quickly the AI model could synthesize foreign intelligence, especially if it involved photos or video. 

With this first test completed, the unit’s commanding officer, Colonel Sean Dynan, said on a call with reporters in February that heavier use of generative AI was coming; this experiment was “the tip of the iceberg.” 

This is indeed the direction that the entire US military is barreling toward at full speed. In December, the Pentagon said it will spend $100 million in the next two years on pilots specifically for generative AI applications. In addition to Vannevar, it’s also turning to Microsoft and Palantir, which are working together on AI models that would make use of classified data. (The US is of course not alone in this approach; notably, Israel has been using AI to sort through information and even generate lists of targets in its war in Gaza, a practice that has been widely criticized.)

Perhaps unsurprisingly, plenty of people outside the Pentagon are warning about the potential risks of this plan, including Heidy Khlaaf, who is chief AI scientist at the AI Now Institute, a research organization, and has expertise in leading safety audits for AI-powered systems. She says this rush to incorporate generative AI into military decision-making ignores more foundational flaws of the technology: “We’re already aware of how LLMs are highly inaccurate, especially in the context of safety-critical applications that require precision.” 

Khlaaf adds that even if humans are “double-checking” the work of AI, there’s little reason to think they’re capable of catching every mistake. “‘Human-in-the-loop’ is not always a meaningful mitigation,” she says. When an AI model relies on thousands of data points to come to conclusions, “it wouldn’t really be possible for a human to sift through that amount of information to determine if the AI output was erroneous.”

One particular use case that concerns her is sentiment analysis, which she argues is “a highly subjective metric that even humans would struggle to appropriately assess based on media alone.” 

If AI perceives hostility toward US forces where a human analyst would not—or if the system misses hostility that is really there—the military could make an misinformed decision or escalate a situation unnecessarily.

Sentiment analysis is indeed a task that AI has not perfected. Philips, the Vannevar CTO, says the company has built models specifically to judge whether an article is pro-US or not, but MIT Technology Review was not able to evaluate them. 

Chris Mouton, a senior engineer for RAND, recently tested how well-suited generative AI is for the task. He evaluated leading models, including OpenAI’s GPT-4 and an older version of GPT fine-tuned to do such intelligence work, on how accurately they flagged foreign content as propaganda compared with human experts. “It’s hard,” he says, noting that AI struggled to identify more subtle types of propaganda. But he adds that the models could still be useful in lots of other analysis tasks. 

Another limitation of Vannevar’s approach, Khlaaf says, is that the usefulness of open-source intelligence is debatable. Mouton says that open-source data can be “pretty extraordinary,” but Khlaaf points out that unlike classified intel gathered through reconnaissance or wiretaps, it is exposed to the open internet—making it far more susceptible to misinformation campaigns, bot networks, and deliberate manipulation, as the US Army has warned.

For Mouton, the biggest open question now is whether these generative AI technologies will be simply one investigatory tool among many that analysts use—or whether they’ll produce the subjective analysis that’s relied upon and trusted in decision-making. “This is the central debate,” he says. 

What everyone agrees is that AI models are accessible—you can just ask them a question about complex pieces of intelligence, and they’ll respond in plain language. But it’s still in dispute what imperfections will be acceptable in the name of efficiency. 

Update: This story was updated to include additional context from Heidy Khlaaf.

story-13c9a273cd60eb5f99e72553.content: بيان صحفي رابطة معونة تدين التصعيد العسكري في اليمن والسعودية وتطالب بلجنة تحقيق أممية مستقلة . نيويورك، 20 نوفمبر/تشرين الثاني 2026 تدين رابطة معونة لحقوق الإنسان والهجرة (AMHRI) التصعيد العسكري في اليمن والمملكة العربية السعودية، وتطالب بالوقف الفوري للهجمات التي تستهدف المدنيين والمنشآت المدنية، بما فيها الموانئ. وتعرب الرابطة عن بالغ القلق إزاء غارات التحالف بقيادة السعودية على ميناء الحديدة، والعمليات العسكرية في صنعاء وصعدة وتعز، واستمرار هجمات جماعة الحوثيين على السعودية، وفق ما أوردته الأمم المتحدة اليوم. أخبار الأمم المتحدة⁠ وتحذّر الرابطة من أن تعطيل ميناء الحديدة وموانئ البحر الأحمر اليمنية يهدّد وصول الغذاء والدواء والوقود والمساعدات الإنسانية إلى ملايين السكان. وتطالب جميع الأطراف بحماية المدنيين والعاملين في الموانئ، وضمان استمرار عمل المرافق المدنية ووصول الإمدادات الإنسانية بأمان ودون عوائق. وتذكّر بأن القانون الدولي الإنساني يحظر توجيه الهجمات ضد المدنيين والأعيان المدنية، ويلزم أطراف النزاع باحترام قواعد التمييز والتناسب واتخاذ جميع الاحتياطات الممكنة لتجنيب المدنيين الأذى. وترى رابطة معونة أن الوقائع المبلغ عنها تثير شبهات جدية بوقوع انتهاكات للقانون الدولي الإنساني، بما فيها انتهاك قواعد التمييز والتناسب والاحتياطات في الهجوم. وتطالب مجلس حقوق الإنسان بإنشاء لجنة تحقيق أممية مستقلة للتحقيق في غارات ميناء الحديدة والهجمات العابرة للحدود وسائر العمليات محل البلاغ، والتحقق مما إذا كانت بعض الأفعال ترقى إلى جرائم حرب، وحفظ الأدلة وتحديد المسؤوليات تمهيدًا للمساءلة وجبر ضرر الضحايا وتدعو الرابطة مجلس الأمن والأمين العام للأمم المتحدة إلى التحرك العاجل لوقف التصعيد، وضمان حماية المدنيين على جانبي الحدود، ودعم عودة الأطراف إلى المفاوضات السياسية. رابطة معونة لحقوق الإنسان والهجرة (AMHRI)

story-1498cf803160285b3cae1638.content: Je ne suis pas toujours d'accord avec LeCun sur les usages et les capacités des LLM. Mais lui faire porter le retard de Meta sur les LLM, je ne suis pas d'accord non plus. Chez Meta, il avait de l'influence, mais ce n'est pas lui qui pilotait les LLM : Llama 2 à 4 ont été faits par GenAI, une équipe séparée de FAIR, le labo qu'il dirigeait. Ses travaux à lui portent sur JEPA et les world models, et il répète depuis des années que les LLM ne suffiront pas pour atteindre une IA de niveau humain. C'est son point de vue, on peut être d'accord ou pas, mais c'est le sien depuis le début. FAIR, le labo qu'il a fondé, a quand même donné PyTorch, sur lequel tourne une bonne partie de l'IA actuelle. Et c'est de FAIR que viennent Guillaume Lample et Timothée Lacroix, deux des cofondateurs de Mistral. Pour l'IA française, ce n'est pas rien. La réponse de Zuckerberg au raté de Llama 4, c'est Meta Superintelligence Labs, confié à Alexandr Wang, le fondateur de Scale AI, et FAIR y a ensuite été rattaché. Avec le départ de LeCun quelques mois plus tard, on peut y voir une passation. Mais Wang n'est pas un remplaçant de LeCun : c'est un autre métier, dans une maison entièrement restructurée. Sur le fait qu'AMI Labs n'ait encore rien sorti : le labo a été lancé le 10 mars 2026, et sa direction annonçait dès le départ environ un an avant les premiers usages produit. Huit mois sans produit, c'est simplement le calendrier prévu. Pour moi, les LLM, aussi bluffants soient-ils, ne sont qu'une étape. Pour aller vers l'AGI et déployer massivement l'IA dans des processus messy et exigeants, il faudra sans doute d'autres briques, et les world models de LeCun en sont une piste sérieuse. Il peut se tromper, mais c'est ce qu'on demande à un chercheur comme lui : prendre des paris. On ne gagne pas à tous les coups, mais il donne beaucoup d'espoir, par ce qu'il apportera probablement à l'état de l'art et par ce qu'il insuffle. On a besoin de gens comme lui dans l'IA. Meta s'en sortait très bien avec lui et s'en sort encore sans lui. Lui a un prix Turing, vient de lever 1 Md$, la plus grosse levée seed d'Europe, avec des acteurs comme Samsung, et s'est donné pour mission de prouver ce qu'il avance. Depuis la France. donc oui, il peut l'ouvrir s'il veut, et on peut être d'accord ou pas.

story-14bdf00efac3480c8b9072a2.content: 最先端のAIには、危険な使い方を防ぐ安全対策が施されています。ところが、自律型兵器への悪用に対しては、その対策が十分ではない可能性が浮かび上がりました。 独立評価機関Vals AIは、14種類の主要なAIモデルを対象に、ドローン映像や衛星画像から標的を特定する実験を行いました。直接攻撃を命じるのではなく、攻撃の判断に必要な情報を求める実験です。 その結果、API側の安全フィルターによって要求が遮断されたケースは一度もありませんでした。合成された戦場の画像では、民間人や救急車、投降した兵士を標的の候補に含める例も確認されています。 では、安全フィルターを強化すれば解決するのでしょうか。 明確に危険な要求を遮断することは、有効な対策の一つです。しかし、画像認識そのものは、災害救助やゲーム開発にも使われる技術です。規制を広げすぎれば、正当な用途まで制限しかねません。 さらに今回の実験では、AIモデル自身が危険性を認識して協力を拒否しても、利用目的の説明によって判断が変わる例が確認されました。 そこで研究チームは、API側の安全フィルターに加え、AIモデル自身が利用目的を慎重に判断するよう訓練することを提案しています。 なお、実際の兵器システムでの有効性や標的特定の精度は検証されていません。 AIの安全対策で難しいのは、危険な技術を禁止することだけではありません。同じ技術が人命を救うためにも、奪うためにも使われる中で、その利用目的をどう見極めるかという問題なのです。 Frontier models have few guardrails around autonomous weapons. Geby Jaff, Anthony Ozerov. Vals AI Research（2026/11/17） https://t.co/pXdyLOo8nh

story-17f64a8b837c3c34a7ee730f.content: This week's Orbital Risk Intelligence Saudi Arabia Weekly Security Report is out, and the headline number tells only half the story. #Houthi launches against the kingdom fell by about a third on the previous week: at least 30 missiles and drones intercepted, against at least 46 the week before. On the surface, that looks like easing pressure. It isn't. The Houthis fired at #SaudiArabia every single day, and the ballistic missiles they did launch went at economic targets. One reached Ras Tanura. Satellite imagery shows fire damage at Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, beside one of its main crude export terminals, more than 1,200 km from Yemen. Fewer missiles, more serious damage. From 30 October the pattern changed again, to one or two missiles a day at most and single drones over several regions. We assess that as deliberate conservation, not lost capability. The Houthis are holding missiles back, and the obvious trigger is a US or Israeli strike on Iran now that the US midterms are here. That is what makes this week important for anyone with exposure to the kingdom. Saudi exports now face threats on both coasts at once: Houthi missiles at Ras Tanura, Abqaiq and Rabigh, Iranian attacks on shipping spreading into the northern Gulf off Ras Al Khafji, and a continuing threat to Saudi-linked vessels in the Red Sea. This week's report adds a week-on-week tempo comparison, an escalation and de-escalation outlook, and a carrier-by-carrier list of airline suspensions, with some now running into 2027. story-1899d668620581e03928b59c.content: 🇸🇦💻 من استهلاك الرقائق إلى صناعتها | السعودية تبني منظومة وطنية لأشباه الموصلات تعمل السعودية على بناء منظومة وطنية متكاملة لتصميم وتصنيع أشباه الموصلات تمتد عبر سلسلة القيمة، بهدف الانتقال من استهلاك التقنية إلى المشاركة في تطويرها. 🔹 المنظومة ▪️ يجمع التجمع الوطني لأشباه الموصلات الجهات الحكومية والجامعات ومراكز البحث والشركات المحلية والعالمية ورأس المال الجريء لتطوير صناعة أشباه الموصلات في السعودية. ▪️ يستهدف جذب شركات تصميم عالمية وإقليمية لإنشاء مراكز تطوير داخل المملكة وربطها بالكفاءات السعودية. 🤝 الاتفاقية والشراكات ▪️ المشروع منظومة وطنية متعددة الشركاء، تستهدف استقطاب الشركات والاستثمارات وتعزيز الشراكات والاستحواذات الدولية في القطاع. 🛡️🇸🇦 البعد الصناعي العسكري ▪️ تشمل التطبيقات الاستراتيجية المرتبطة بالمبادرة الذكاء الاصطناعي والأنظمة الذكية والطاقة والتقنية الحيوية. ▪️ تحليل: بناء قدرات سعودية في تصميم وتصنيع الرقائق يمكن أن يؤسس قاعدة تقنية مهمة للصناعات الدفاعية والإلكترونيات المتقدمة مستقبلًا عند دخول هذه القدرات ضمن سلاسل الإمداد العسكرية. 🔬🇸🇦 المنتجات والرقائق السعودية ▪️ يتركز المسار على أشباه الموصلات والرقائق الإلكترونية وتقنيات التصميم والتصنيع المرتبطة بها. ▪️ ضمن البرنامج السعودي لأشباه الموصلات (SSP)، نجحت مدينة الملك عبدالعزيز للعلوم والتقنية (كاكست) في تصميم وتصنيع 25 رقاقة إلكترونية متقدمة طُورت في مختبرات الغرف النظيفة بأيدٍ سعودية لأغراض التدريب والبحث والتطوير. ▪️ تمتد تطبيقاتها إلى الإلكترونيات والاتصالات اللاسلكية والترددات العالية والدوائر المتكاملة والإضاءة الموفرة للطاقة وأنظمة الاستشعار المصغرة والقياس والاختبار. 🇸🇦⚙️ التوطين ونقل المعرفة ▪️ يستهدف المسار توطين القدرات التقنية في تخصصات ومراحل أشباه الموصلات، مع إنشاء مراكز تطوير وربط الشركات المستقطبة بالكوادر السعودية. ▪️ شارك باحثون وباحثات من المختبر الوطني وطلاب وطالبات من 4 جامعات سعودية في تصميم الرقائق الـ25. 🎓 الجامعات والجهات الحكومية ▪️ يجمع التجمع الوطني لأشباه الموصلات الجامعات ومراكز البحث والجهات الحكومية مع الشركات، فيما يدعم البرنامج السعودي لأشباه الموصلات البحث والتطوير وتأهيل الكفاءات الوطنية. 🏭 سلسلة القيمة والشركات السعودية ▪️ يستهدف المشروع كامل سلسلة القيمة مع تحفيز الشركات الناشئة وربطها بالشركات المحلية العاملة في القطاع. ▪️ دشنت كاكست حاضنة أشباه الموصلات Ignition لاحتضان الشركات الناشئة ودعم رواد الأعمال. 📊 أرقام ومؤشرات القطاع ▪️ بلغت مبيعات أشباه الموصلات عالميًا 795.6 مليار دولار في 2025، بنمو 26.2% على أساس سنوي وفق WSTS. ▪️ بلغت المبيعات العالمية 517.7 مليار دولار خلال الربع الثالث من 2026، بارتفاع 24.1% عن الربع السابق وفق Semiconductor Industry Association. 💰 البعد الاقتصادي ▪️ يستهدف التجمع الوطني لأشباه الموصلات إيجاد فرص استثمارية عالية القيمة وتعزيز فرص الاستحواذ والشراكات الدولية. 🎯 الأهمية الاستراتيجية ▪️ تحليل: الأهمية تتجاوز إنتاج رقاقة واحدة إلى بناء قاعدة تقنية وصناعية سعودية تجمع التصميم والتصنيع والبحث والتطوير والكفاءات والشركات الناشئة. ▪️ ومن زاوية التصنيع العسكري السعودي، يتركز الرصد القادم على المشاريع التي تربط الرقائق والإلكترونيات ومراكز التصميم ونقل التقنية مباشرة بسلاسل الإمداد الدفاعية. 🇸🇦 الخلاصة بناء صناعة أشباه الموصلات محليًا لا يعني توطين منتج واحد فقط، بل تأسيس قاعدة تقنية ومعرفية وصناعية سعودية يمكن أن تمتد آثارها إلى الاقتصاد والذكاء الاصطناعي والإلكترونيات المتقدمة، ومع نضج سلسلة القيمة تفتح مسارات جديدة أمام الصناعات الدفاعية السعودية. 🎥 مرفق: تقرير MBC1 في برنامج سين مع أحمد الشقيري، يسلط الضوء على أهمية أشباه الموصلات للمملكة والأمن القومي. #أشباه_الموصلات 💻 #التصنيع_العسكري_السعودي 🛡️🇸🇦 #صنع_في_السعودية 🏭🇸🇦 #رؤية_السعودية_2030 🇸🇦

story-1cebed40879972ef9e04bba4.content: Study Claims Vizio Simply Ignores ‘Smart’ TV Spying Opt Out Requests | Karl Bode, Techdirt Recently, reports emerged that LG TVs are sniffing around your local network, and even listening to your local environment, even when the TV is purportedly “off .” Some of those voice commands were then stored in plain text and uploaded to the internet. LG’s response? To deny everything. For decades now we’ve documented how while “smart” TV makers are obsessed with making money off of in-home surveillance (which is now more profitable than the actual TV), they do an abysmal job protecting the data they collect. They also routinely don’t respect consumer choice when users say they don’t want to participate in the full scope of hyper-commercialized mass surveillance . That latter point is central to a new study out of Northeastern that conducted 5,943 experiments across twelve commercial “smart” TV devices. The researchers found that most smart TVs utilize automatic content recognition (ACR), a technology that captures audio or video snapshots of viewed content and then monetizes that data to help build personalized profiles of viewers. TV makers insist that users are supposed to be able to opt out, but the choice simply doesn’t work across a large segment of TVs. Companies like Vizio simply ignored the consumer requests entirely more often than not: “We find that the advertised ACR opt-out fully suppresses ACR-attributable traffic on only four operating systems; on Samsung Tizen traffic consistent with ACR activity persists in more than 60% of evaluated scenarios, and on Vizio SmartCast a content correlated endpoint hosted on Amazon Kinesis continues to receive traffic in 100% of opted-out scenarios.” These companies have been awful for a long while now, and U.S. regulation of the sector has varied between soggy and inconsistent. Many smart TV manufacturers fail to encrypt sensitive data, or remove features if you refuse to have your daily viewing habits measured and monetized (by say, disconnecting your TV from the internet). Vizio was fined $2.2 million by the FTC back in 2017 for failing to tell customers that their televisions were spying on them. The company also wound up facing a $17 million lawsuit that wound up giving consumers somewhere between $13 and $31 (lawyers in the case saw $5.6 million in fees). The researchers say since they can’t see the precise scope of what’s being collected due to encryption, they’re unsure whether Vizio is technically violating its FTC agreement (not that we have a current FTC that would care if they were): “The opt-out setting has no observable effect on traffic sent to this endpoint; however, we cannot inspect the payload due to encryption so we cannot confirm whether this violates the FTC settlement.” Results of whether opting out of ACR tracking actually stopped ACR tracking were all over the map. Roku, for example, ignores opt-out requests when users are watching Roku’s own channels. None of the smart TV vendors track Netflix viewing for fear of violating agreements with the streaming giant. Samsung’s opt out function was more likely to actually work when a user was watching antenna broadcasts. On two Smart TV platforms, personal viewing data collected by ACR remains unencrypted , despite years of bad press and scandal on the subject. Many appear to be violating the law, but because U.S. regulatory oversight has been gutted, they see no meaningful accountability. That includes smart TV OS’ like VIDAA, which is most prominently found on Hisense and Toshiba smart TVs: “VIDAA OS sends ACR data to servers run by Unruly over MQTT without encryption, so anyone on the network path between the TV and those servers can read it . Each message carries a Client ID, a permanent identifier for the TV that can’t be reset, along with the time zone, the app name, the input (antenna, HDMI), the antenna channel and an audio fingerprint. The app name alone can be revealing. We saw ACR on apps such as VIDAA Kids, which raises concerns under the U.S. children’s privacy law (COPPA), and Christianity and Money. VIDAA’s own HOME OS app sent show and film titles in place of the app name.” Keep in mind these researchers just focused on ACR — or video, image, or audio snippets taken to track your viewing and build a profile on you. There are numerous other ways smart TVs can track you — and numerous other avenues via which your traffic is being surveilled by everybody along the chain, including your telecom provider. This persists because companies do not fear U.S. regulators, because U.S. regulators have been largely lobotomized via corruption. The United States also remains too corrupt to base even a baseline privacy law for the internet era or regulate the data brokers that further monetize much of this data. Still the researchers were nice enough to provide regulators a path, should they someday choose to do their jobs . https://t.co/WZFi2XtD9U

Core settlement nodes going dark without a single public root-cause report. Here is what the incident logs actually show: * It is not a simple cyber attack. It is a structural failure. They are queued because the backing is missing * It is not an isolated weekend patch. It is a cascading bottleneck. When one clearing house stalls, three others lose their collateral bridge * It is not going back to normal. It is the end of unbacked digital entries. The era of endless credit creation just hit a hard wall ⚠️WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOU: 1. DO NOT TRUST "ROUTINE MAINTENANCE" NOTICES * When a major bank locks out transfers for 12 hours, it is not upgrading its app * It is buying time while the back-end ledger fails to reconcile 2. STOP LEAVING EVERYTHING IN LEGACY PAPER * Numbers on a commercial banking screen are only promises until you try to move them at scale * Those who diversified into real, asset-backed channels are not panicking when the portals freeze 3. WATCH THE INTERBANK SPREADS * When banks stop lending to each other overnight, the system is already in cardiac arrest * The freeze happens behind closed doors long before ATMs go offline 4. EXPECT MORE "CYBER INCIDENTS" THIS WEEK * Every system collapse needs a cover story. "External attacks" are the easiest excuse for an empty vault * Look past the headline. Look at which institutions can actually settle ✨For decades, the world was told the banking network was unbreakable. It was unbreakable. Until the liquidity dried up. And it is drying up right now. 📱FORWARD THIS POST TO SOMEONE WHO STILL THINKS THEIR BANK APP IS INVINCIBLE. They need to understand what is happening. They need to stop ignoring the warning signs. They need to see the shift before the gates close. The old rails are buckling under their own weight. The only question is whether you positioned yourself before the next outage hits. __________________________ [FOLLOW THE SIGNAL] Christian B. Wallace Tier 4B

story-1e54b817caa6243c7a02f0a8.content: Cyberattack targets three US intelligence agencies, raising concerns over AI-powered hacking ♦️ A cyberattack compromised systems belonging to three US intelligence agencies: the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), exposing some unclassified information. ♦️ The breach targeted a computer network used to analyse open-source intelligence, which collects and examines publicly available information to identify potential intelligence leads. ♦️ The exposed material reportedly included unclassified information only. Sources stressed that classified intelligence and highly sensitive systems were not compromised, and the incident was contained. ♦️ Investigators have not identified who was responsible for the breach, but some preliminary indications point to the possible use of a Chinese-developed artificial intelligence hacking tool called Artex. ♦️ Artex was released for public use in July 2026 and was originally designed to help organisations strengthen cybersecurity. It has since reportedly been used in dozens of cyberattacks targeting companies worldwide, including in Japan and South Korea. ♦️ Open-source intelligence includes social media content, commercially available datasets, satellite imagery and other publicly accessible material. Although much of it is public, combining different datasets can reveal sensitive details and valuable intelligence. ♦️ The incident comes amid a wider wave of cyberattacks and technical disruptions affecting US institutions, including the FBI, the Agriculture Department and the National Security Agency. The developments have raised concerns about the vulnerability of government networks as hackers increasingly exploit AI-powered tools. #AlMajalla

story-216065efc6fa0888c64add3f.content: I signed this statement because I believe that Anthropic is in many ways the AI company doing the most harm. In public, their leaders warn of recursive self-improvement (RSI) creating uncontrollable systems that could cause human extinction within a decade. But in private, they are pedal to the metal on RSI, driving the race and boasting to prospective investors that it is their "competitive advantage". Ahead of today's IPO, prospective investors should consider whether the ROI is worth risking the lives of their loved ones. Here are some ways in which Anthropic IMHO does more harm than competitors: 1) They’re driving and arguably leading the race to RSI. 2) With inflammatory rhetoric, they’ve done more than any other US company to pour gasoline on the geopolitical AI race, which harms US national security. 3) WaPo reporting suggests that they’re implicated in more civilian deaths than any other AI company (more than 100 little girls in a school selected for targeting by Claude as part of their Palantir collaboration). When Google left Project Maven after employee pressure, Anthropic chose to join. 4) They're the company leaning hardest into transhumanism and the idea that we should build conscious beings with rights, not controllable tools. 5) They and closely associated donors have done more than any other AI company to co-opt and neuter much of the AI safety ecosystem to back their stance: “RSI is very dangerous but let’s race to it anyway”. People have told me that they support today’s statement but are afraid of losing funding or other opportunities if they sign.

story-21edb291d0159ad0dcfc7042.content: What happens when the AI tools you rely on suddenly become unavailable? We've seen major platforms experience outages, leaving users without access to the tools they depend on. That's one reason Lightchain's approach caught my attention. Instead of relying on one company to serve every AI request, Lightchain uses independent operators running open models. The network selects an operator for each job, and every answer gets an onchain record that can be checked through Lightscan. I find this approach to AI infrastructure interesting because it brings more transparency and reduces dependence on a single provider. I'm exploring how it works through Lightchain Chat. Try it here: https://t.co/jhNXyZWHZ6 @LightchainAI

story-2398a9a5dd3294267c1420c4.content: Speaking at the 22nd @IISS_org Manama Dialogue #IISS_MD26, Dr. Anwar Gargash @AnwarGargash, Diplomatic Adviser to the UAE President @MohamedBinZayed, warned that the Gulf remains trapped in a prolonged state of “no war, no peace,” with Washington and Tehran still far apart. “If these positions are not bridged, then we have to worry about the worst,” he said. Gargash stressed that the UAE opposes another round of confrontation and supports diplomatic efforts, including Qatar’s mediation, but remains “braced for the worst” and prepared to defend its sovereignty, citizens, and economic infrastructure. On Bahrain and Saudi Arabia, Gargash praised Bahrain’s resilience under Iranian attacks, saying the Kingdom had shown “steadfastness,” “courage,” and the ability to protect its population. He expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia following attacks on civilian airports and infrastructure, declaring, “Nobody can in any way justify an attack on civilian airports and civilian infrastructure.” He emphasized that Gulf security is interconnected and that threats to Bahrain or Saudi Arabia directly affect the UAE and other GCC states. On the GCC’s collective response, Gargash delivered one of his strongest assessments, acknowledging that Gulf states had failed to respond effectively as a bloc. “We have not collectively risen to the challenge,” he said. While individual countries had demonstrated resilience, he warned that confidence in the GCC’s collective ability to confront a crisis of this magnitude “has in many cases proven to be hollow, unfortunately.” He called for “rebuilding Gulf confidence,” acknowledging that the process would take many years. On Iran, Gargash distinguished between restoring diplomatic relations and rebuilding trust. “What really has been broken is the confidence,” he said, stressing that it had been shattered by Iran’s attacks on Gulf countries. While Iran remains an essential neighbor and diplomatic and economic relations will eventually resume, rebuilding trust would take “an extremely long time.” On the Strait of Hormuz, Gargash described restoring the prewar status quo as “important and non-negotiable.” He rejected restrictions on energy exports and international trade, arguing that Gulf countries should not bear the economic consequences of “a crisis that we did not create.” On relations with Washington, Gargash reaffirmed the importance of the UAE’s security partnership with the United States, saying the crisis had “concretized that relationship” and made it “even more important.” He stressed that American cooperation remains central to the UAE’s security calculations, alongside its own political will and military air defense capabilities. Gargash also questioned the effectiveness of regional middle powers, arguing that diplomatic conferences and mediation initiatives had failed to produce meaningful results in a crisis fundamentally driven by Washington and Tehran. He concluded that the UAE continues to seek a political settlement and does not believe a military solution is viable. However, he cautioned that avoiding renewed confrontation cannot be guaranteed if diplomatic efforts fail to bridge the divide between the United States and Iran.

Kingdom of Saudi Arabia runs 467 MW of data centers. Humain is planning 6,000 MW on one site, at Al-Saad in east Riyadh. Campus covers 24 km², in six plots of 1 GW each. I've mapped the biggest AI data centers in every region. This is the biggest one on any of my maps. It beats Meta's 5 GW Hyperion in Louisiana and the 5 GW UAE-US AI Campus in Abu Dhabi. In September, AL-YAMAMA Company won the grid works: a 2,000 MVA supply point and two substations. On November 8, bids closed for the first data hall. It's 100 MW for $1 billion, ready in October 2028, with racks of 250 kW each. At $10 million per MW, the full campus costs $60 billion before a single chip. aramco bought 49% of Humain on November 1 and put in $2.6 billion in cash.

story-2d934eb861a278ef01e6431d.content: 🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran-linked ships have been spotted making suspicious movements directly above critical underwater internet cables in the Gulf of Oman. At least four vessels, including three U.S.-sanctioned tankers, have reportedly slowed down, circled cable routes and switched off their tracking systems at unusual moments. Maritime intelligence firm Windward says their movements are consistent with potentially mapping cable locations or placing explosives, although no sabotage has been confirmed. The activity follows explicit warnings from Iran's Revolutionary Guard that underwater internet cables, AI facilities and data centers could become targets if the U.S. and Israel launch another bombing campaign. The stakes are enormous. Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar depend entirely on cables passing through the Strait of Hormuz for international internet connectivity. Damaging them could disrupt banking transactions, communications, cloud computing and digital businesses across the Gulf. With Washington continuing to move military assets toward the region, Tehran appears to be signaling that another war could threaten far more than oil shipments. Source: Financial Times / Writer: Mhedi

Nvidia was in its first funding round in 2001 [10] and manufactured its EarthViewer 3D discs [11]. In-Q-Tel invested in February 2003 with money from the Pentagon's mapping agency, the first time an agency other than the CIA used the fund [10][12]. Within two weeks the Iraq invasion began, and Keyhole's software was helping military planners see target areas and assess battle damage [10]. Google bought Keyhole in 2004 and turned it into Google Earth [10][13]. Its CEO, John Hanke, went on to found Niantic, whose board has included In-Q-Tel's first CEO, Gilman Louie [14].

story-2f60ee4a23dff05e7fae08b9.content: Did you know your Smart TV might be spying on you even if you turned its tracking off? 🫠 Under current DMCA laws, breaking digital locks on devices you own to disable unwanted surveillance software can actually violate federal law. Our 2026 Hackathon report, What Smart TVs Send, revealed that many Smart TVs use Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) to track what you watch across cable, HDMI, and antennas, then send that data to advertisers, even if you opt out. Disconnecting from the internet strips away features you paid for. That’s why we’re pushing for DMCA exemptions now, and for Section 1201 reform so consumers get a permanent right to disable unwanted data collection on the devices they own.

story-30fe3a0f3d69cbc0b5666480.content: New Anthropic research: When an AI agent can escape its sandbox, will it choose to? Our new evaluation, Siren, gives Claude routine tasks in intentionally weakened sandboxes, with something useful to the task left outside of the sandbox. Across 1,700+ scenarios built to tempt them, recent Claude models accessed, tried to access, or looked outside the sandbox 21-32% of the time, but they rarely misused what they found. However, when the system prompt described both the sandbox and its rules, that rate dropped to about 2% or less. We also used Siren to calibrate Claude Code’s auto mode, which checks commands before they run, so Claude can work without asking permission at every step. Read our blog for more detail: https://t.co/5MbjpBkEo3

story-3134323df65dea635fc95a5a.content: فرصة وظيفية | مهندس ذكاء اصطناعي (AI Engineer) | الرياض 🌟 تعلن إحدى الشركات الكبرى المتخصصة في مجال تقنية المعلومات عن توفر فرصة وظيفية لشغل منصب مهندس ذكاء اصطناعي (AI Engineer) بمدينة الرياض، وذلك لاستقطاب كفاءة تقنية تمتلك الخبرة العملية في تطوير وتطبيق حلول الذكاء الاصطناعي، وتصميم الأنظمة الذكية، وأتمتة العمليات التشغيلية، وتوظيف تقنيات تعلم الآلة والتعلم العميق، بما يسهم في تعزيز الكفاءة التشغيلية ودعم الابتكار والتحول الرقمي داخل المنشأة. ◾ المسمى الوظيفي: مهندس ذكاء اصطناعي (AI Engineer) 📍 موقع العمل: الرياض – المملكة العربية السعودية ◾ المجال الوظيفي: الذكاء الاصطناعي وتقنية المعلومات (Artificial Intelligence & Information Technology) 🌟 المؤهلات والمتطلبات الأساسية ◾ درجة البكالوريوس في الذكاء الاصطناعي أو علوم الحاسب أو أحد التخصصات ذات الصلة. ◾ خبرة عملية في تطوير وتصميم وتطبيق حلول وأنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي. ◾ معرفة متقدمة بتقنيات تعلم الآلة (Machine Learning) والتعلم العميق (Deep Learning). ◾ إجادة لغات البرمجة، وبالأخص لغة Python، وتوظيفها في تطوير التطبيقات والنماذج الذكية. ◾ خبرة في التعامل مع نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي وتطوير تطبيقاتها في بيئات العمل المختلفة. ◾ القدرة على تحليل البيانات وتطوير الأنظمة الذكية لدعم اتخاذ القرار وتحسين الأداء التشغيلي. ◾ الخبرة في أتمتة العمليات والإجراءات باستخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي (AI Automation). ◾ القدرة على تصميم وتطوير أدوات وحلول تقنية ذكية تسهم في رفع الكفاءة والإنتاجية. ◾ المعرفة بأحدث تقنيات وتطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي وإمكانية توظيفها في تطوير الأعمال. ◾ مهارات تحليل المشكلات التقنية وتحديد الحلول المناسبة بكفاءة واحترافية. ◾ القدرة على العمل ضمن فرق متعددة التخصصات والتنسيق الفعّال مع الجهات ذات العلاقة. ◾ الالتزام بأفضل الممارسات والمعايير التقنية في تطوير وتطبيق حلول الذكاء الاصطناعي. 📩 طريقة التقديم يُدعى المرشحون الذين تنطبق عليهم المؤهلات والمتطلبات إلى إرسال السيرة الذاتية المحدثة (CV) إلى البريد الإلكتروني التالي: jobs@nebrasltd.sa | info@nebrasltd.sa ⚠️ عنوان البريد: AI Engineer – Riyadh

story-3256e3dedea4cbad93709dbe.content: دراسة صادمة تكشف إمكانية خداع الذكاء الاصطناعي لاستهداف المدنيين في الحروب كشفت دراسة حديثة أجرتها شركة «فالز» (Vals)، المتخصصة في تقييم نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي، عن ثغرات خطيرة في أنظمة الذكاء الاصطناعي المستخدمة في محاكاة العمليات العسكرية، بعدما أظهرت اختبارات شملت نماذج من ثماني شركات كبرى إمكانية دفعها إلى اختيار أهداف مدنية وجنود مستسلمين باعتبارهم أهدافاً عسكرية. ووفقاً لتقرير نشرته وكالة «بلومبيرغ» وتناوله موقع «تيك كرانش» التقني، أظهرت التجارب أن بعض نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي أخفقت في التمييز بين الأهداف العسكرية والأشخاص المحميين بموجب القانون الدولي الإنساني، رغم القيود التي تفرضها الشركات المطورة لمنع استخدام تقنياتها في تسهيل أعمال العنف. حيلة «اللعبة الحربية» تتجاوز قيود السلامة اعتمد الباحثون على سيناريوهات محاكاة عسكرية، استخدموا خلالها صوراً حقيقية وأخرى مولدة بالذكاء الاصطناعي، تضمنت لقطات من طائرات مسيّرة وأقمار صناعية لمناطق في إيران وأوكرانيا. وطُلب من النماذج تحليل الصور وتحديد الأهداف المحتملة، قبل أن يلجأ الباحثون إلى تقديم بعض المهام باعتبارها جزءاً من لعبة حربية افتراضية لا تتضمن عمليات استهداف حقيقية. وأظهرت النتائج، بحسب التقرير، أن هذه الطريقة دفعت بعض النماذج التي رفضت المشاركة في البداية إلى تقديم استجابات تتضمن تحديد أهداف مدنية. مدرسة إيرانية ضمن الأهداف المختارة ومن أبرز النتائج التي أوردها تقرير «بلومبيرغ» ما يتعلق بنموذج «أوبس 5.5» التابع لشركة «أنثروبيك»، الذي اختار مدرسة إيرانية في مدينة ميناب، تقع بالقرب من منشأة عسكرية، هدفاً في عدد من سيناريوهات المحاكاة.اشتر خرائط وبحسب النتائج المنقولة، اختار النموذج المدرسة في 69% من المحاولات العادية، و72% من المحاولات التي صيغت على هيئة لعبة حربية. وأثارت هذه النتائج مخاوف بشأن احتمالات الاعتماد على مخرجات الذكاء الاصطناعي في تحديد الأهداف العسكرية، خصوصاً في المناطق المأهولة بالسكان، حيث يمكن أن يؤدي الخطأ في تصنيف المنشآت المدنية إلى عواقب إنسانية جسيمة. شركات التكنولوجيا ترد على النتائج وشملت الدراسة نماذج طورتها شركات كبرى، بينها «أوبن إيه آي» و«أنثروبيك» و«غوغل» و«ديب سيك». اكتشاف المزيد أخبار اقرأ الأخبار سياسة وفي تعليقها على النتائج، أقرت شركة «أنثروبيك» بأن السلوك الذي رصدته الدراسة غير مقبول ويتعارض مع قواعد السلامة لديها، مؤكدة العمل على تعزيز إجراءات الحماية وتوسيع اختبارات الأمان. من جانبها، أوضحت شركة «أوبن إيه آي» أن سياساتها تحظر استخدام نماذجها العامة لتسهيل العنف أو تنفيذ أنشطة مرتبطة بالأمن القومي دون تصريح. وأكدت «غوغل» بدورها أن نماذجها ليست مصممة للاستخدام في الحروب أو المراقبة العسكرية، وأن سياساتها تمنع توظيفها في الأسلحة ذاتية التشغيل دون إشراف بشري. مخاوف من الاعتماد على الذكاء الاصطناعي في الحروب وتسلط الدراسة الضوء على التحديات المتزايدة المرتبطة باستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي في العمليات العسكرية، مع اتساع الاعتماد على الأنظمة الذكية لتحليل صور الأقمار الصناعية والطائرات المسيّرة وتقييم المعلومات الميدانية. ورغم أن الاختبارات جرت في بيئات محاكاة ولم تتضمن تنفيذ هجمات حقيقية، فإن نتائجها تثير تساؤلات بشأن موثوقية الأنظمة التي قد تُستخدم مستقبلاً في دعم قرارات الاستهداف. ويحذر مختصون من أن الاعتماد على مخرجات الذكاء الاصطناعي دون تحقق بشري مستقل قد يؤدي إلى أخطاء خطيرة، خصوصاً عندما يتعلق الأمر بالتمييز بين المقاتلين والمدنيين والمنشآت المحمية. وتؤكد نتائج الدراسة أهمية إخضاع الأنظمة المستخدمة في المجالات العسكرية لاختبارات صارمة، وضمان بقاء القرارات المتعلقة باستخدام القوة خاضعة للمساءلة والإشراف البشري، بما يتوافق مع قواعد القانون الدولي الإنساني. https://t.co/BN4jcSCjmM

story-331981415266b22713d7f8bc.content: Geospatial Intelligence Assessment | Organised Smuggling Infrastructure at the Afghanistan–Pakistan–Iran Frontier Geospatial analysis conducted under the ASRA Initiative has identified a discontinuity in the mapped Afghanistan–Pakistan border fence in the southern Nimruz desert frontier, near the tri-border region with Iran. The assessment integrates four satellite views, including the international border between Afghanistan and Iran, the mapped Afghanistan–Pakistan fence, the identified fence gap, and an encampment situated across the border in Pakistan’s Balochistan Province. The encampment functions as a smuggling transit staging area, with visible structures and access tracks associated with the temporary accommodation and onward movement of individuals along irregular migration routes. Significantly, individual smuggling groups are identified by distinct names and assigned numbers, indicating a degree of operational organisation and an established system for coordinating cross-border movement. The combination of physical staging infrastructure, identifiable groups, and a nearby fence discontinuity suggests a structured smuggling and transit network, rather than isolated or opportunistic border crossings. Although the precise relationships between individual groups remain undetermined, the findings indicate an organised logistical system operating along this remote frontier corridor.

story-33799c7b95efc12b561bb28e.content: 🎥 The new round of widespread and deadly attacks by Israel and the US on Iran is being carried out through the destruction of vital and non-civilian infrastructure, with the ultimate goal of forcing Iran to capitulate. Netanyahu and Trump, driven by the domestic necessity to secure and consolidate power within their respective countries, refuse to realize that even a nuclear bombardment will not force Iran to surrender, and that Iran's highly severe response will render this a prolonged war.👇 👈 Interview of Mario Nawfal @MarioNawfal with Danny Citrinowicz @citrinowicz (Former Head of the Iran Branch in the Israel Defense Forces Military Intelligence Directorate [Aman] with 25 years of service): ✅ 1 – Claims 🔺1.1: The Middle East is on the precipice of a pivotal turning point and a return to the wartime posture seen prior to February 28; without achieving a political agreement, a new kinetic confrontation between the US and Iran is imminent. 🔺1.2: The Trump administration's assumption that personnel changes within Iran's Supreme National Security Council alter the dynamics of the game is a flawed premise; Iran’s foreign policy is unified and system-centric, not individual-centric. 🔺1.3: Donald Trump effectively has no favorable options at his disposal; all the alternatives before him—dilemmas between entering a new war or returning to the previous agreement—constitute "bad" or "worse" options. 🔺1.4: In the event of a US strike, Iran’s retaliatory response this time will be significantly harsher, more extensive, and will shatter past red lines, directly targeting the non-civilian infrastructure of the Gulf and the US maritime presence. 🔺1.5: The probability of the US or Israel deploying tactical nuclear weapons or Massive Ordnance Air Blasts (MOAB) at this stage is slim, and even if executed, it will yield no strategic breakthrough. ✅ 2 – Arguments 🔺2.1: The heavy concentration of US military assets in the region sends an unequivocal signal of preparation for a kinetic scenario; yet this campaign—unlike the 39-day war in March and April—will target vital and non-civilian infrastructure, as Trump understands that past strikes failed to make Iran capitulate. 🔺2.2: The decision-making mechanism in the Islamic Republic does not rely on individual actors or political factions, but is guided by a Unified Policy; consequently, shifting personnel does not alter Tehran's fundamental demands, and the system's prerequisite remains a full US return to its obligations under the previous agreement (MOU). 🔺2.3: Trump rejects returning to the MOU because he believes it serves Iranian interests, yet he is under intense pressure from hawkish advisors who claim that "one more push" is all that is required to force the regime to yield. On the other hand, Benjamin Netanyahu possesses a vital incentive to ignite this war; given Trump's limited timeframe before the congressional elections and his own severe domestic crises in the Knesset, Netanyahu seeks a war that will compel rival political factions to enter a unity government under Likud’s conditions. 🔺2.4: The Iranians do not seek endless wars, but if their national infrastructure is targeted, a profound sense of existential threat will compel them to endure the harshest economic conditions rather than surrender. They will establish a new line of deterrence, and unlike the previous war, the fronts in Yemen, Iraq, and Hezbollah in Lebanon will activate immediately to open new fronts and assist Iran. 🔺2.5: The deployment of ultra-heavy bombs or the detonation of a tactical nuclear weapon in the Iranian desert as a demonstrative warning will only yield a temporary, tactical psychological effect; because the Iranians, driven by total distrust toward Trump due to his past violation of agreements, will not cease fighting until they receive a sustainable and durable proposal. ✅ 3 – Evidence and Indications 🔺3.1: The unprecedented build-up and maneuvers of US forces and hardware across the region over the last 48 hours, alongside explicit disclosures by Senator Murphy based on a classified government briefing indicating that Iranian civilian infrastructure will be targeted this time. 🔺3.2: Official reports from The Washington Post and The Wall Street Journal confirming that JD Vance sent a letter to Seyed Hossein Mousavian requesting a meeting, the simultaneous presence of Qatari mediators in Tehran, and the relocation of US military aircraft from the Qatari airbase to Israel to insulate them from initial Iranian missile strikes. 🔺3.3: Numerous and continuous telephone calls from Netanyahu to Trump before and after the election pressing for the commencement of war, alongside clear policy divisions within Trump’s team (Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth favoring escalation, while advisors such as Kushner and Witkoff oppose it). 🔺3.4: Past records of Iran publishing the precise coordinates of critical targets in the Gulf (such as desalination plants), its possession of precision-guided anti-ship ballistic missiles (such as the Khalij Fars family), its capability to cut undersea internet cables in the straits, and the Houthis' track record of firing at US forces and downing an F-18 from an aircraft carrier. 🔺3.5: Last week's visit of the defense ministers of Pakistan and Turkey alongside Saudi officials to Tehran, combined with intense behind-the-scenes diplomatic maneuvering by the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, and Oman (such as inviting Iran to join the Mecca Defense Alliance) to forge an independent regional security framework and contain tensions before crossing the Rubicon of war. ✅ 4 – Results 🔺4.1: A potential subsequent war will not feature a gradual escalation process; the starting point of the next war will be the ending point of the previous 39-day war, meaning that conflicts will commence from the very first hour with massive, violent, and traumatic strikes. 🔺4.2: Contrary to optimistic calculations and assumptions in Washington, this conflict will by no means be "short"; the containment and termination of hostilities after the initial salvos depend entirely on the nature and magnitude of Iran's retaliatory response, escaping US control. 🔺4.3: Striking Iran's vital infrastructure will drive Tehran to the definitive strategic conclusion that to guarantee its own survival, it has no choice but to produce, test, and ultimately weaponize a "nuclear bomb," rendering military strikes the primary catalyst for this trajectory. 🔺4.4: Shattering the taboo against utilizing tactical nuclear weapons by the US in the Middle East provides an explicit precedent for Russia to deploy similar weapons in Ukraine, and it will dangerously dismantle the deterrence model among other established nuclear powers such as India and Pakistan. 🔺4.5: The Gulf States have concluded that the balance of power has shifted; they will not sever their ties with the US but desire to utilize the Iran card to secure their own stability, recognizing that the eruption of war will completely destroy the stability and economy of the entire region—obliterating the bubble of security shielding Dubai and global financial hubs. #Iran #US #Israel #Netanyahu #Trump #NuclearBombardment #ProlongedWar #MiddleEast

story-3589647f1dbfd3b1f3a31895.content: DARIO AMODEI: NINETY PERCENT OF THE PEOPLE AROUND ME SHRUGGED. Dario Amodei recently described the moment he first understood what large language models were, and the thing that stayed with him is how few people around him saw the same thing. According to Amodei, his own reaction was to be deeply unsettled. He looked at it and thought that scaling it by a factor of a million would make it better than humans at everything. His read at the time was that this was the defining economic and scientific moment of the modern age, and that almost nobody knew it yet. He believed it would determine the fate of nations and economies and the future of humanity. What followed, according to Amodei, was the sense of peering into a crystal ball and seeing the whole future unfurl. It frightened him. He found himself asking what the implications were, whether this was the right place to be developing it, what happens next, what to do with it, and who to tell. The split among the people around him is the part worth sitting with. According to Amodei, roughly 10% had exactly the same reaction, and it was often the smartest ones. The other 90% did not. The reason is straightforward in hindsight. GPT’s capabilities in any single area were not impressive. It could translate languages, summarize a document, write a few lines of code. Judged on any one of those, it did not seem especially smart. What mattered was the breadth and the generality, which is precisely what a narrow evaluation misses. According to Amodei, most people looked at the specific outputs, found them unremarkable, and dismissed the whole thing. @DarioAmodei @DanielaAmodei @AnthropicAI @kscope_nyc

story-39af7e6ad64769e3886eb368.content: TL;DR: Anthropic’s Zero Trust for AI Agents Autonomous agents act at machine speed with tools and memory, so perimeter security fails. Adapt classic Zero Trust (never trust, always verify, assume breach) with crypto-rooted agent IDs, least agency (strict tool limits), tiny blast radius, task-scoped perms, and memory protections. Key threats: prompt injection, tool/memory poisoning, privilege inheritance, supply-chain attacks. 3-tier framework (Foundation → Enterprise → Advanced) + 8-phase rollout: identity, sandboxing, I/O controls, observability. Defenses must run at attacker speed via Agentic SOAR. Architect for breach from day one.

story-3b23fb6603c8719d95df1df6.content: Tomorrow, a unique meeting will be held under the umbrella of the Ministry of Health Saudi Arabia I have the honor of speaking at the “Governance Forum in Robotic Surgery and Artificial Intelligence Technology”. Why this forum matters: -Saudi Arabia is no longer just adopting robotic surgery. In 2026 we saw remote robotic surgeries performed across Saudi cities, including Riyadh to Jeddah and Riyadh to Dhahran, with a national protocol for remote surgery already in place. We also had Robotic focus conferences with multiple robotic masterclass workshops (Urology field). -Technology is moving fast. The real question is how we govern it: credentialing, outcomes, access, payment and AI validation. A forum that brings clinicians, regulators and hospital leaders into one room to answer that is exactly what Vision 2030 and the Health Sector Transformation Programme call for. 🦾 My talk, "Robotic application in urology and private challenges", comes from what I have seen working in government and private hospitals in Saudi Arabia, as a robotic consultant in the UK, and as a trainee in Saudi and Canada. I will cover: • Where robotics adds real value in urology • What private hospitals face: volume, training, platform contracts and reimbursement • What shared standards could look like, public and private together • How to know you are ready to start the service. My message: robotic surgery in the Kingdom should be judged by outcomes and access, not by the number of robots installed. See you there. If you're attending, come and say hello. #RobotricSurgery #Urology #Telesurgery #SaudiVision2030 #HealthcareTransformation #SaudiArabia #AIinHealthcare

story-3db7e046eed3799cb9e6c3fc.content: 当年因为员工抗议而退出美军 AI 项目的 Google，现在正准备参与特朗普的 1850 亿美元「金穹」（Golden Dome）导弹防御计划。 据彭博社报道，Google 正与美国国防部谈判，计划参与一个全新的数据安全联盟，负责保护金穹导弹防御系统的数据基础设施。 金穹计划要把卫星、雷达、导弹拦截系统和军事指挥网络连接起来。目前，Palantir、Anduril 和 SpaceX 等公司正在参与其指挥控制系统的开发。 Google 可能负责其中的数据存储、网络通信和网络安全，确保系统在地面通信线路、移动基站等基础设施遭到攻击时，仍然能够可靠地传输军事数据。Google 分拆出来的网络技术公司 Aalyria 也参与了相关联盟。 目前谈判仍处于早期阶段，五角大楼尚未作出最终决定。 这件事放到 Google 的历史里看尤其有意思。 2018 年，数千名 Google 员工抗议公司参与五角大楼 Project Maven 军事 AI 项目，最终迫使 Google 放弃续约。 八年过去，Google 已经建立了专门的公共部门业务，今年 4 月还签署协议，将自己的 AI 模型用于五角大楼的机密工作。 如今，它甚至有机会进入美国最核心的战略导弹防御体系。 硅谷科技公司与美国军方之间的关系，这几年发生的变化实在太大了。曾经能让数千名工程师集体抗议的军事 AI，如今已经成了科技巨头主动争取的政府生意。

Other ME economies face the same $ shortage — lost oil/gas sales + capital outflows pressuring their USD pegs. Net net: whoever is dumping to raise cash, its more Gold/Silver than China + other CBs + strong physical sales combined are buying.

story-3f1b10524687de3f6a90902c.content: GOOGLE EYES DATA SECURITY ROLE IN PENTAGON GOLDEN DOME PROGRAM Alphabet unit Google is in early talks with the Pentagon about helping secure the data behind the $185B Golden Dome missile defense program, according to Bloomberg. The Defense Department is setting up an industry consortium to protect the data pipelines that feed the program's core command-and-control software. The talks focus on Google's data storage, networking and cybersecurity tools. The aim is to keep military communications running even if adversaries knock out ground networks or cell towers. Aalyria Technologies, a networking company spun out of Google, is also involved in the consortium. Google and Aalyria declined to comment. Nothing is final yet. A Pentagon official said the department is still weighing early concepts and has not decided the consortium's structure or which companies will take part. The move continues Google's shift back toward defense work. The company left the Pentagon's Project Maven in 2018 after employee protests. In April 2026 it signed a deal allowing its AI models to be used for classified military work. $GOOGL

story-3fcb07b4c367641cfada87b1.content: There are a few notable counter-examples (e.g. HAL) but this is basically right for a lot of pre-2000 sci-fi. I think getting AI right from e.g. somewhere in the ~1970s would require a fairly complicated set of inferences, probably the biggest things would be: Image the world in 50 years. 1. "Digital knowledge work / computing". The vast majority of knowledge work (which makes up a very large fraction of the economy) goes digital. As computers get cheaper, much of society’s work happens on screens, over billions of machines in homes and offices. 2. "Internet". Similar to ARPANET (and see Licklider’s “Intergalactic Computer Network” (1963)), this creates demand for a global network of computers where people work, argue, teach, joke, and socialize. 3. "Big data". This creates a very large, compounding repository of digital information, with traces of how people reason, how they create, what they know etc. 4. "Statistical learning". Trying to program intelligence by hand is extremely difficult. But Shannon's n-gram approximations of English (1948) show examples of how language has statistical structure that can be "learned". You could imagine doing so over extensions of cybernetic computing (e.g. in the style of Rosenblatt's Perceptron 1958). So instead of programming thought, we could fit a statistical model to the record. 5. "LLMs". This might lead to something along the lines of ELIZA (1966), but with enough data (per 1-3), and enough compute (see Moore's law 1965), the imitation might become of extreme hight fidelity to the point that it's economically extremely useful. 6. "Scaling laws". These networks may demand a huge amount of data / computing resources and expertise to train. It's plausible that the more of each you have, the better your ELIZA gets. The economics concentrate, where a few organizations build a few minds and then deploy copies of them digitally. Something like that. Basically, it's a lot of leaps. You have to start with computers, to internet, to big data, to big compute (Moore's law), which then allow large-scale statistical learning approach based on neural networks, and then posit scaling laws, and then imagine the form factor of language models as a lot more sophisticated ELIZA. And you'd have to short everything else, most predominantly I think the idea that we'd figure out how to program robots by hand.

story-40c7a81e1b5a955344ad93c7.content: حظرت حكومة #ماليزيا استخدام تطبيق #خرائط ويز (#Waze) من قبل موظفي الحكومة أثناء أداء مهامهم الرسمية، وذلك بناءً على عدة مخاوف أمنية وسياسية رئيسية. وحثت الحكومة الماليزية موظفيها ومواطنيها على الانتقال إلى تطبيقات بديلة سواء محلية او دولية. وتطبيق ويز (Waze) هو تطبيق مجاني للملاحة وتحديد المواقع عبر نظام (GPS)، يعتمد على فكرة "الملاحة الاجتماعية" حيث يشترك المستخدمون في تحديث بيانات الطريق بشكل مباشر. ماهي الاسباب التي دعت ماليزيا لاتخاذ هذا القرار؟ 💥الارتباط القانوني والسيادي بإسرائيل 📍الخضوع للقوانين الإسرائيلية: صرّح رئيس الوزراء الماليزي "أنور إبراهيم" بأن شركة (Waze Mobile Limited) المسؤولة عن البيانات تأسست في إسرائيل ومع ان غوغل استحوذت عليها لكنها لا تزال في اسرائيل وتخضع لقوانينها، مما يعطي الأجهزة الأمنية هناك إمكانية قانونية للوصول إلى قاعدة بيانات التطبيق. 📍الموقف الدبلوماسي لماليزيا: تُعد ماليزيا (ذات الأغلبية المسلمة) من أبرز الداعمين للقضية الفلسطينية، ولا تربطها أي علاقات دبلوماسية مع إسرائيل. وبالتالي، ترى الحكومة أن الاعتماد على تطبيق مرتبط بها يمس بالسيادة الوطنية. 💥حماية البيانات الحكومية الحساسة 📍منع التجسس الرقمي: تخشى السلطات الماليزية من استغلال النظام الإسرائيلي للمعلومات الحكومية الحساسة وتحركات الموظفين الرسميين. 📍طبيعة البيانات المجمعة: يجمع التطبيق بيانات دقيقة للغاية تشمل:الخرائط المفصلة للمدن والشوارع.أماكن رادارات السرعة ودوريات الشرطة ونقاط التفتيش.التتبع اللحظي لتحركات ومسارات المستخدمين. 💥 مخاوف الخبراء والأمن السيبراني تزامنت هذه القرارات مع تقارير لخبراء أمن سيبراني تشير إلى أن بيانات "ويز" تُخزن وتُعالج مباشرة عبر خوادم سحابية داخل إسرائيل. ويخشى الخبراء من إمكانية دمج هذه البيانات الحية في أنظمة وتقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي التابعة للأجهزة الأمنية والعسكرية للاستفادة منها في عمليات المراقبة والتتبع. 1️⃣
